Turkey is debasing its currency on purpose now.

The lira has dropped close to 1% or more almost every month this year, and the slide accelerated after April. Ankara is now letting it fall faster on purpose, betting a steady bleed beats a sudden devaluation. This is what chronic currency debasement looks like up close.

Suppress rates and print, and the currency pays the bill. Turkey has run that experiment for years, and the lira keeps finding new lows.

tweets.text:
It took longer to rebuild one Oxford road bridge than it took to build the Titanic.

Botley Road's bridges ran 41 months and roughly $314 million inflation-adjusted. That is more than the Titanic, Disneyland, the Eiffel Tower, and the Space Needle each cost to build, and longer than the Titanic's 36 months.

When a wealthy country can't replace a road bridge for less than the price of the Titanic, the drag isn't money. It is the machine. Western public spending buys less every year.

Russia cannot pump its share of oil anymore.

Russia's crude output ran about 1.3 million barrels a day below its OPEC+ quota in September, and the shortfall keeps widening. Sanctions, Ukrainian strikes on refineries, and aging fields are grinding production lower even as the group raises targets.

Less Russian oil on the market puts a floor under energy prices. That is an energy shock building in slow motion, and it lands at the pump.
